sections.name: Alligator
sections.card:
Summary: The alligator, a big reptile, lives in Bayou Nwa, Bluewater Marsh and parts of Scarlett Meadows. Once its jaws clamp your torso, you die within moments.
Weak points: A rifle shot or thrown tomahawk to the head kills it, and a scope keeps you far away. A bow with poison or improved arrows to the head also works.
Tips: Kill it on the shore, since you cannot skin an alligator in water. Most lie still there until you get close, and a horse ridden at one throws you.

sections.name: Boar
sections.card:
Summary: A wild boar, most common across Lemoyne and also found in New Hanover and West Elizabeth. It drops a boar pelt, tender pork loin, animal fat and a boar tusk.
Tips: Both a rifle and a bow can give a perfect pelt, using poison or ordinary arrows. A boar cannot be stored on your horse, because it is skinned the way elk and bison are.

sections.name: Snake
sections.card:
Summary: Snakes live nearly everywhere, most thickly in the east around Bluewater Marsh and Bayou Nwa. Most are venomous, and they drop stringy meat, snake skin and a snake carcass.
Tips: Only a bow with small game arrows gives a perfect skin, and a Health Cure removes venom. Any perfect snake skin makes the Rattlesnake Vaquero Saddle at the Trapper.

sections.name: Lemoyne Raiders
sections.card:
Summary: A Lemoyne gang that often robs and kills, mostly around Scarlett Meadows, Rhodes and Saint Denis. Their crimes often succeed, thanks to their manpower and ammunition, which other gangs lack.
Looks like: Grey uniforms in the old Confederate army style, each with a yellow neckerchief.
Tips: Under the rail bridge near Hill Haven Ranch, 8 to 12 mounted Raiders can ambush you without warning. Near Catfish Jacksons, they can hit you with a wagon-mounted Gatling gun and reinforcements, with little cover. Certain Raiders at random camps let you keep two hats, the Military Officer's Hat and Military Forage Cap.

sections.name: Murfree Brood
sections.card:
Summary: A cruel, territorial gang found around Roanoke Ridge in New Hanover. You usually meet them robbing a camp of travellers.
Looks like: Often shirtless.
Tips: Their Volcanic Pistols and double-barreled shotguns make close fights deadly, and they can survive a point-blank shotgun blast. Looting them mostly gives cigarettes, tonics and herbs, but ones in scripted ambushes always carry money. You can also loot throwing knives from them.

sections.name: Dynamite
sections.card:
Summary: Thrown dynamite hits very hard but has low range and low accuracy. You can carry up to 8, and you cannot customize it.
Uses: Blowing up a train's engine leaves it inoperable, and it can kill some NPCs you normally cannot target. Fish blown out of the water are poor quality and cost you a little Honor.
Tips: Every fence sells it after "Who the Hell is Leviticus Cornwall?", and some missions give it out. A Volatile Dynamite pamphlet is in a chest at Hani's Bethel, and fences sell it after "American Distillation". Shooting dynamite or a crate of it sets it off, and you can craft arrows that explode.

sections.name: Fire bottle
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown fire bottle with high power but low range and low accuracy. It cannot be customized.
Uses: Like dynamite, it can kill certain NPCs that you normally cannot target.
Tips: Every fence sells it after "The Fine Joys of Tobacco", and you can loot one off enemies earlier. A maxed ammo cart gives two, and the Volatile version does more damage. Its pamphlet is in a chest at a burned-forest campsite northwest of Horseshoe Overlook.

sections.name: Tomahawk
sections.card:
Summary: The tomahawk is a throwing weapon with moderate power but low range and low accuracy. It cannot be customized.
Uses: Thrown at an alligator's head, it kills the animal instantly.
Tips: Every fence and the Trapper sell it after "The First Shall Be Last". Earlier, you can take one at Six Point Cabin before "Paying a Social Call". You can also find one on broken stagecoaches around Southern Cumberland Forest.

sections.name: Throwing knife
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown knife with moderate power and accuracy but low range. It cannot be customized.
Uses: Equipped and aimed at an aggressive enemy up close, it can start an instant takedown. A hunting knife cannot do that.
Tips: "Paying a Social Call" gives you your first, and a fence or the Trapper sells more afterwards. A poisoned one, made at a campfire with Oleander Sage, kills any NPC and scares off dangerous animals. Poisoned knives turn plain once recovered; the improved knife, made with rare bird feathers, may kill outright.

sections.name: Sawed-off shotgun
sections.card:
Summary: A two-shot shotgun with high power but low range and low accuracy. Unlike other shotguns, it sits in your handgun slot.
Uses: Two of them, dual wielded, work very well against people and animals alike.
Tips: Your first one comes in "Enter, Pursued by a Memory", and a second costs $85 at any gunsmith.

sections.name: Cattleman Revolver
sections.card:
Summary: Your starting revolver, a solid all-rounder that holds six rounds. It has moderate power and range, and high accuracy and fire rate.
Uses: Rifling adds range, and a long barrel with better sights adds accuracy. A head, neck or upper-chest shot kills a person outright; torso shots can take three or four.
Tips: You can buy a second at any gunsmith or take one from slain NPCs. At Honor rank +4 or higher, any gunsmith sells the Hero's Pearl Grip for this gun alone.

sections.name: Bolt Action Rifle
sections.card:
Summary: A rifle with five rounds, high power and range, very high accuracy and a slow rate of fire. It costs $180.
Uses: Put a scope on it and it stands in well for the Carcano Rifle.
Tips: Chapter 3's "Preaching Forgiveness as He Went" gives you one, and every gunsmith sells it afterwards. Killing a bounty hunter in "The First Shall Be Last" gets you one earlier. Lawmen at public executions in Valentine and Saint Denis may carry one.

sections.name: Carcano Rifle
sections.card:
Summary: A sniper rifle: six rounds, high power, very high range and accuracy, quick reload, slow fire. It costs $190.
Uses: Its overall stats beat every other weapon, but it only shines when targets are far away.
Tips: It is free in "The Delights of Van Horn" and "Goodbye, Dear Friend", then every gunsmith sells it. The camera view does not matter: you always aim it down the sights.

sections.name: Pump-Action Shotgun
sections.card:
Summary: The Lancaster pump-action shotgun: moderate power, low range, low accuracy, five rounds. It costs $148.
Tips: Any gunsmith sells it after "Pouring Forth Oil IV". Chez Porter has a free one in a weapon case, up the ladder in the master bedroom.
